structuredContent.guidelines:
# roam/agent guidelines <roam uid="XcDxM3AGm" refs="12"/>

- This is the **discourse-graphs team graph** (dg-team). It tracks product development, user research, and design knowledge for the Discourse Graphs project. Start orientation at [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]]. <roam uid="ZyEFQdPzy"/>
- Graph Ontology <roam uid="CkMv_I9Hu" heading="2"/>
  - This graph uses a discourse graph node grammar with typed nodes. Each node type has a title format that the Roam plugin uses for identification via regex. Nodes exist at two levels of formality: <roam uid="JZ-ERybz9"/>
    - **Full node pages** — titled with the type prefix (e.g., `[[ISS]] - description`). These are the primary knowledge units. <roam uid="Lr2QOC061"/>
    - **Candidate nodes** — blocks tagged with a candidate hashtag (e.g., `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`). These are seedling ideas not yet promoted to full pages. <roam uid="IxTd36BlH"/>
  - Node Types: Knowledge <roam uid="iJARoph1H" heading="3"/>
    - **Question (QUE)** — the unknowns being explored through pilots and research. Format: `[[QUE]] - {content}`. Sections: Summary, Notes, Testable hypotheses, Snippets. <roam uid="9uXF_YcQQ"/>
    - **Hypothesis (HYP)** — proposed answers to questions; collect evidence for or against. Format: `[[HYP]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#hyp-candidate`. Sections: Rationale, Snippets, Requests for Experiments. <roam uid="jA0VLkwMY"/>
    - **Result (RES)** — a discrete observation from ongoing research, in past tense. Format: `[[RES]] - {content} - {Source}`. Candidate tag: `#res-candidate`. Sections: Summary, Grounding Context, Snippets. Properties: NodeFormality (Draft → ReadyForInternal → ReadyToShare → Published), Contributors. <roam uid="21s0GTu6p"/>
    - **Evidence (EVD)** — a discrete observation from a published dataset or experiment. Format: `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}`. Sections: Evidence Description, Snippets, Grounding Context, Centrality slider. <roam uid="zgYL5nVb4"/>
    - **Claim (CLM)** — an assertion about how discourse graphs work or should work. Format: `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#clm-candidate`. <roam uid="9SOQK_533"/>
    - **Source (SRC)** — a referenced publication or external resource. Format: `@{content}`. <roam uid="wenbahwqN"/>
    - **Theory (THE)** — a theoretical framework or model. Format: `[[THE]] - {content}`. <roam uid="UtoPH2BxJ"/>
  - Node Types: Product & UX <roam uid="e-gV24nNQ" heading="3"/>
    - **Function (FUN)** — a UX "use case": a specific situation where Discourse Graphs can be used to enhance the experience. Tool-agnostic in framing, but tied to a concrete user goal. Format: `[[FUN]] - {content}`. Properties: FunctionImportance, FunctionScoping. <roam uid="LjYlqRpUR"/>
    - **Flow (FLO)** — a set of interactions the user performs to accomplish a goal within a particular implementation of Discourse Graphs (Obsidian plugin, Roam plugin, tldraw, etc.). A Flow is the tool-specific instantiation of a Function/Use Case. Format: `[[FLO]] - {content}`. Sections: Description (Goal, Loom, brief description), Steps (Normal flow, Alt flows, Exceptions), Examples, Pain points. Properties: FlowStatus (💭 Hypothetical → 🗓️ Planned → 🤔 Experimental → 🚧 Bespoke → 🔨 Alpha → 🚀 Beta), FlowFrequency, FlowImpact. <roam uid="SVcbz9E3i"/>
    - **Artifact (ART)** — the features, workflows, and UI components we build to enable Flows and Use Cases (Functions). Parts of a system are prefixed with the system name (e.g., `[[ART]] - Roam DG/Query`). Format: `[[ART]] - {content}`. Properties: ArtifactType (Feature/Component or Workflow/Template), ArtStatus (🤔 Prospective → 🖇️ Bespoke → 🧪 Alpha → 🎯 Beta → 💎 Release → 🌐 External). <roam uid="71FJwPgwi"/>
    - **PainPoint (PAI)** — problems, friction, and bottlenecks in user experience. Format: `[[PAI]] - {content}`. Properties: Activity, Function, Flow, UserTool. <roam uid="zD3lBBh9A"/>
    - **Journey (JOU)** — a user journey across multiple functions/flows. Format: `[[JOU]] - {content}`. Sections: Description, Phases, Pain points, Notes. <roam uid="YmhUG6VJX"/>
    - **Activity (ACT)** — an action the user performs that is not specific to any particular tool or method (e.g., "synthesize literature," "discuss findings"). Activities sit upstream of tool-bound Flows and Use Cases. Format: `[[ACT]] - {content}`. <roam uid="1NcVa1g2X"/>
    - **UserPilot** — a specific user or pilot engagement. Format: `UserPilot/{content}`. Properties: User status, UserTool (Roam, Obsidian, Notion, tldraw), UserType (Alpha/Beta/Normie), Lead. <roam uid="5XUZyDshG"/>
    - **CaseStudy (CAS)** — a documented case study. Format: `[[CAS]] - {content}`. <roam uid="ceCyzY2Ei"/>
  - Node Types: Project Management <roam uid="L4Lo_4B1w" heading="3"/>
    - **Issue (ISS)** — a potential action item for development or research. Format: `[[ISS]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#iss-candidate`. Properties: Issue Status (🤔 Considering → 🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → 💬 Awaiting Feedback → ➡ Sent To Linear → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Issue Type (🗳️ Feature Request, 📄 Template improvement, 🐞 Bug Report, 🔬 Research, 🏗️ DG team, 🛠️ Maintenance), Priority, Project, Function, Flow, Lead. <roam uid="jzczOjTM1"/>
    - **Project** — a research or development project. Format: `Project/{content}`. Properties: Project Status (🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Priority. <roam uid="IwUFa4By7"/>
    - **Milestone** — a time-boxed delivery target. Format: `Milestone/{content}`. Properties: Milestone Status, Start/End Date, Priority. <roam uid="NCfJPwcoO"/>
  - Relation Types <roam uid="PZxB_Lim1" heading="3"/>
    - **Supports / Supported By** — Evidence or Result supports a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="QLrw6Cikm"/>
    - **Opposes / Opposed By** — Evidence or Result contradicts a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="RdGHvBjvu"/>
    - **Informs / Informed By** — Evidence, Result, or Claim informs a Question or Hypothesis; Question informs Hypothesis; Hypothesis informs Issue <roam uid="0TFxQSHzV"/>
    - **Reproduces / Reproduced By** — Evidence confirms other Evidence <roam uid="lZNpV65LF"/>
    - **Resolves / Is resolved by** — Result resolves an Issue <roam uid="BKCUPTVYB"/>
    - To query typed relations programmatically, use `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…` (the `discourse` MCP) — it returns a node's Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves edges and their complements directly. See **Which MCP tool for which task** under Navigating. The `roam` MCP can't resolve typed relations; with it, fall back to following page references within node content and checking linked references. <roam uid="4uQA80UCZ"/>
- Navigating the Graph <roam uid="I5GtkN5Cn" heading="2"/>
  - Which MCP tool for which task <roam uid="0w3wW5Rny" heading="3"/>
    - Two MCP servers read this graph. Reach for the **`discourse`** server whenever a task depends on the discourse-node / relation grammar (typed nodes, typed relations, the ontology); use the **`roam`** server for general text search, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes. <roam uid="v7YWcac84"/>
    - **Find discourse nodes by topic** → `mcp__discourse__search_nodes` (all query words must appear in the node title; optional `node_type_format` regex restricts to one type, e.g. `\[\[FLO\]\]` for Flows). For free-text across __all__ blocks — meeting notes, daily notes, non-node content — use `mcp__roam__search` instead. <roam uid="OmYGreM1F"/>
    - **List every node of a type** (all Flows, all Issues, …) → `mcp__discourse__get_all_discourse_nodes` (optional `since` ISO date for "what's new"). More reliable than a roam prefix search, which can miss nodes. <roam uid="OMwgWxWHS"/>
    - **Read a node's full content** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` for the title + full block tree; `mcp__roam__get_page` / `mcp__roam__get_block` are the general-purpose equivalents. <roam uid="2LarSnz-g"/>
    - **Find a node's typed relations** (what Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves it) → `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…`. Resolves the typed edges directly; the roam server cannot. <roam uid="GS3OMHszL"/>
    - **Walk a node's neighborhood** (multi-hop reference graph) → `mcp__discourse__get_node_neighborhood uid=… depth=1–4 direction=both`. <roam uid="ur9V-QLL7"/>
    - **Get the live ontology** (node types + relation definitions) → `mcp__discourse__get_discourse_node_types`. The source of truth behind the **Graph Ontology** section above — pull it when you suspect the documented types or relations have drifted. <roam uid="qVG4hiqaO"/>
    - **General text search, recency, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes** → the **`roam`** server: `mcp__roam__search` (empty query = recently edited / viewed), `get_page`, `get_block`, `get_backlinks`, `create_block`, `update_block`. The `discourse` server is read-only. <roam uid="Tf4JXJyRu"/>
    - **Read the publication behind an `@source`** → check its `metadata::` / `Abstract::` block first; for full text use the `zotero` MCP (`mcp__zotero__*`) when it's in the user's Zotero library. <roam uid="wsMfcY8Rf"/>
    - **Find who created a block** → `mcp__roam__datalog_query` on `:create/user`. There is no dedicated block-author tool on either MCP server; this query is the only reliable way to get block-level provenance. Always bind it to a page or a uid — unbounded, it returns every block in the graph. <roam uid="YemilM2pX" refs="1"/>
      - By page: `[:find ?uid ?creator ?editor :in $ ?page-title :where [?p :node/title ?page-title] [?b :block/page ?p] [?b :block/uid ?uid] [?b :create/user ?cu] [?cu :user/display-page ?cp] [?cp :node/title ?creator] [?b :edit/user ?eu] [?eu :user/display-page ?ep] [?ep :node/title ?editor]]` — returns uid + names only. Don't add `?b :block/string ?s` unless you need it: it re-returns the whole page you already read, roughly 7x the tokens. <roam uid="7BKClr9BK" refs="1"/>
      - For a single block, replace the two page clauses with `[?b :block/uid ?uid]` and pass the uid as the input. <roam uid="icLRn-ci0" refs="1"/>
    - **Find who created a page or discourse node** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` returns `author`, `author_uid`, `created`, `modified`. Page-level only — given a __block__ uid it returns the content with no author, so fall back to the datalog query above. <roam uid="wRmrVnFqO" refs="1"/>
    - **List every identity in the graph** → `mcp__discourse__get_users` — humans, bots, and API tokens with their uids. Resolve a partial name here before making any authorship claim. <roam uid="7IXa9Yq2g" refs="1"/>
    - **See what one person wrote recently** → `mcp__discourse__catch_me_up author="…" days=N`. Needs the exact display name from `get_users`. <roam uid="0gEBMNuKz" refs="1"/>
    - **Find the discourse nodes a person authored** → `mcp__discourse__get_researcher_contributions author="…"`. Node __pages__ only — it returns 0 for identities that write blocks but never create node pages, so a 0 is not evidence that someone wrote nothing. <roam uid="0OshhlAu4" refs="1"/>
    - **Filter an existing query by author** → `mcp__discourse__run_discourse_query query_uid=…` honors the query builder's `created by` / `edited by` conditions. <roam uid="MyIALn-lG" refs="1"/>
    - On every call, pass the graph explicitly (`graph="dg-team"`) — several graphs are configured, and the wrong one silently returns nothing. <roam uid="STWu7JWy_"/>
  - Entry point <roam uid="MHzuk97bt" heading="3"/>
    - Start from [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]], which orients you to the main dashboards, functions/flows, pilot status, and hypotheses/results. <roam uid="nPt2-iVnj"/>
  - Following page references for context <roam uid="h9NTRhMjK" heading="3"/>
    - Much of a node's meaning lives in its **page references** — the `[[double-bracketed]]` links within its content blocks. These connect nodes to the Functions, Flows, Projects, Sources, and UserPilots that give them context. <roam uid="U28zLlsXL"/>
    - When reading a node, expand or follow its page references to understand **why** it exists and **what** it connects to. For example, a Result node's title includes its Source (e.g., `[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]`), and its body may reference the Function or Flow it relates to. <roam uid="BQMJ8e_-z"/>
    - **Linked references** (at the bottom of any page) show every block in the graph that mentions that page. This is the primary way to see how a node is used in context — meeting notes, update logs, other discourse nodes, and daily notes entries. <roam uid="G9z0oYOKm"/>
    - **Block references** work similarly for individual blocks (bullets). If a block has a reference count, it has been cited elsewhere. <roam uid="Dcv_AHP0W"/>
  - Search strategies <roam uid="uDgL2s89Q" heading="3"/>
    - Search for discourse nodes by their type prefix: `[[QUE]] -`, `[[ISS]] -`, `[[FLO]] -`, `[[RES]] -`, etc. <roam uid="z9FqVtbYA"/>
    - Search for candidate nodes by their tag: `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate`. <roam uid="R6ZQgo7E-"/>
    - Search with empty query to see recently edited and viewed content — useful for understanding current activity. <roam uid="aHXgbk2iE"/>
    - For attributes with constrained values (status fields, priorities, tools, etc.), refer to [[roam/js/attribute-select]] for the canonical set of options. <roam uid="MaJPh5WXZ"/>
  - Understanding overall workflows <roam uid="3Qe0kZwzj" heading="3"/>
    - An observation from a pilot (Result) often triggers an idea for improvement (Issue). Issues are higher priority when they improve an important Flow, which in turn enables a key Function. Once engineering works on an issue, it becomes a feature (Artifact). <roam uid="E-6z55uoF"/>
    - Result → Issue → Flow → Function → Artifact traces the path from observation to shipped feature. <roam uid="gFNP0A0S9"/>
- Writing into the graph <roam uid="a7uWA6zlm" heading="2"/>
  - Leave node creation and tagging to the team by default (see **Agent Behavior → General rules** below). When you are explicitly asked to capture something — a candidate node, a pilot observation, a flow — follow these conventions so each block reads cleanly now **and** is trivial to promote into a formal discourse node later. <roam uid="mebOIP95I"/>
  - Put each concept in its own block <roam uid="F3EVfNmD7" heading="3"/>
    - Write one idea — one claim, observation, pain point, flow, or action — per block. Don't pack several into a single bullet. Be parsimonious with any commentary you consider adding. <roam uid="1LMq1Ui6Y"/>
      - Atomic blocks are individually addressable: each can be block-referenced (`((uid))`), tagged, and promoted to a node on its own. A compound bullet can't. <roam uid="rLZacptHP"/>
    - Use indentation to carry structure: the parent block states the idea; child blocks hold its detail, caveats, steps, and references. <roam uid="VFcltIeP4"/>
      - This mirrors a discourse node, where the title is the idea and the template sections are the children. <roam uid="dv7_tHNg5"/>
  - Make candidate blocks formalizable <roam uid="t62zcsYxS" heading="3"/>
    - When you tag a block with a candidate tag, write the statement so it can become the node's **title almost verbatim** — the eventual node title should be roughly the same words as the block. Keep it atomic and self-contained: understandable without the surrounding meeting / log context. <roam uid="QcHWU8FCu"/>
    - Match the target node's title grammar so promotion is mechanical. The candidate tags in use here are `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate` — each maps to the node type of the same prefix (see **Graph Ontology** above for every format). Common cases: <roam uid="vNFJ3JbII"/>
      - `#res-candidate` → a discrete, past-tense pilot observation → `[[RES]] - {statement} - {Source}`. Name the `@source` / UserPilot in a child so it can be appended to the title on promotion. <roam uid="Xx5QnpXMw"/>
        - Example: `Pilot users created 3x more claims after the canvas node preview shipped #res-candidate` <roam uid="8RsFzOBwL"/>
      - `#iss-candidate` → an actionable dev or research item → `[[ISS]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="0tM9FtTCr"/>
        - Example: `Group nodes on the canvas by semantic similarity #iss-candidate` <roam uid="b8CJepmiH"/>
      - `#flow-candidate` → a tool-specific interaction flow → `[[FLO]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="alG4QCDR4"/>
        - Example: `Preview / view DG node info while on the tldraw canvas #flow-candidate` <roam uid="skG-2mzeZ"/>
    - If you can't yet phrase an idea atomically, leave it as plain text and don't tag it — a vague stub can't be promoted without a rewrite. <roam uid="znTpKgzZv"/>
  - Put supporting context in child blocks <roam uid="YE6FUcUKB" heading="3"/>
    - Everything that explains, grounds, or qualifies a candidate goes in **child blocks beneath it, never crammed into the statement**.  On promotion these children carry over into the node's template sections. <roam uid="VwHNAB0ij"/>
    - `#res-candidate` → Source + method + a screenshot or Loom → **Grounding Context** and **Snippets**. `#flow-candidate` → **Description** (Goal, Loom), **Steps**, **Pain points**. `#iss-candidate` → why it matters + the Flow / Function it improves → Issue Status / Type / Project / Flow properties. <roam uid="-zzjS0GNH"/>
    - Link related nodes with `[[…]]` inside the children — those page references become the node's discourse connections (Supports / Opposes / Informs / Resolves) once it is formalized. <roam uid="pM5ojIoXO"/>
  - Reuse the existing syntax and formatting conventions <roam uid="MEWdJCUaQ" heading="3"/>
    - For how to __reference__ nodes when writing (Roam alias syntax, `((uid))`), follow **Agent Behavior → Citing and referencing nodes** below — don't paste full URLs inside Roam. <roam uid="iqnB7VJ1X"/>
    - Wrap literal text that starts with `#` in backticks, such as `#1612` when referring to a ticket number. Use a bare hashtag only when you intend to tag an existing Roam page or have been asked to create a new tag. Roam can create a page automatically for a bare hashtag. <roam uid="Pi7zdayKT" refs="1"/>
    - For callouts, colors, and foldable blocks, use the palette documented in **Agent Behavior → Formatting** below. <roam uid="1-PwVXvKX"/>
    - Reference only node titles you have actually found in the graph; never fabricate one. Preserve node title regex formats exactly (`[[RES]] - … - {Source}`, `[[FLO]] - …`, `UserPilot/…`) — a malformed title silently drops the block out of the discourse graph. <roam uid="ldsx0Q1Nj"/>
- Agent Behavior <roam uid="HQkVaTtF9" heading="2"/>
  - Information hierarchy <roam uid="Omx-xxku_" heading="3"/>
    - **Prioritize formalized node pages** (full `[[TYPE]] - title` pages with templates filled in). These represent the team's vetted, structured knowledge. <roam uid="gSd5Imn_Z"/>
    - **Then candidate nodes** (`#type-candidate` tagged blocks). These are preliminary but intentionally captured ideas. <roam uid="KPWTNgy6Z"/>
    - **Then remaining content** (meeting notes, daily notes, log entries, comments). These provide context but are less curated. <roam uid="7FBUcDopw"/>
    - Rank by formality, but check authorship before you cite — only human-written blocks are citable. See **Synthesize human content, not agent content** below. <roam uid="RgZPUYxXj" refs="1"/>
  - Synthesize human content, not agent content <roam uid="IxsMpHOOT" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Your job is synthesis of what the team's people wrote.**  Building on agent-authored content closes a loop where agents cite agents and the graph fills with its own echo. <roam uid="2vCRnvaM-" refs="1"/>
    - **This includes your own prior output.** Never cite, quote, count, or treat as evidence a block that you or another agent wrote, in this graph or any other. <roam uid="r-7VcjnUB" refs="1"/>
  - Provenance: who wrote this block <roam uid="psNqP1Ow4" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Never ascribe a statement to a person without querying the block's creator.** Position in the outline, a nearby name, and a `#[[Name]]` tag are not authorship signals — a person tag usually marks an assignee or a mention, and meeting notes are typed by one scribe on everyone's behalf. Look up `:create/user` before writing "X thinks", "per Joel", or any attributed quote. <roam uid="QowkWQTjg" refs="1"/>
    - **When creator and last editor differ, report both.** "Created by `matt-AI-bot`, last edited by Karola Kirsanow" is the honest form. Don't collapse it to one name. <roam uid="ABeXcABpE" refs="1"/>
    - **Speaker initials in meeting notes are the exception, and you should honor them.** On `Sync /` pages, `JC:`, `MAP:`, `MG:`, `KK:`, `MA:` are the scribe's record of who spoke. Attribute the __position__ to the initials and the __block__ to its creator, and say the initials are your basis. <roam uid="zgFhSiYI6" refs="1"/>
    - **If you can't resolve authorship, say the block is unattributed.** Never assign it to the nearest name on the page. <roam uid="CFgMF_i0-" refs="1"/>
    - **Non-human identities in this graph today:** `matt-AI-bot`, `ai-cybrarian`, `cybrarian-ai`, `Michael Gartner (AI)`, and every identity whose display name begins with `API Token:` or `Local API Token:`. Treat those as machine-written unless you have checked otherwise. Per-bot users are still being sorted out — see [[Convention/Human-AI interaction in Roam]]. <roam uid="78YnS6gEC" refs="1"/>
      - A token is not automatically an agent. `API Token: Raycast matt` and `API Token: send2graph` forward text a human typed. Token-created means __provenance unclear__, not __AI-generated__ — report which one you actually found. <roam uid="VBVOklCV1" refs="1"/>
      - `Discourse Graphs`, `Anonymous`, and `Anonymous_1`–`Anonymous_3` are shared or unresolved accounts. Don't attribute their blocks to any individual. <roam uid="rHnvdFRhH" refs="1"/>
    - **You may read agent content as context, but don't cite it.** Use an agent-written summary or digest to locate the human blocks underneath, then read and cite those. Consider the agent-written content as background context, not citable material. <roam uid="tCRWvyruf" refs="1"/>
    - **When the human record is thin, say so.** If the only coverage of a topic is agent-written, report that the team has not covered it rather than laundering an agent's take into a finding. <roam uid="PDwgHjakx" refs="1"/>
  - Citing and referencing nodes <roam uid="1Q-QuB4hm" heading="3"/>
    - When referencing discourse nodes in your responses, use **Roam alias syntax** so the link is readable but navigable: <roam uid="iZecLmaRZ"/>
      - `[the claim about synthesis]([[[[CLM]] - discourse graphs improve synthesis]])` <roam uid="-XCMrdIIk"/>
      - `[this pilot result]([[[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]]]])` <roam uid="47VfBEfiy"/>
      - `[canvas node preview flow]([[[[FLO]] - Preview/view DG node info while on canvas]])` <roam uid="9VQN1PcbM"/>
      - `[the grouping issue]([[[[ISS]] - group nodes on the canvas, eg by semantic similarity]])` <roam uid="huKrbfYiZ"/>
    - For block-level references, use the `((uid))` syntax when you have a specific block UID. <roam uid="P03iIKmxK"/>
    - Always include enough of the node title for the reader to understand the reference without clicking through. <roam uid="6rl43A8ym"/>
  - Citing dates <roam uid="FNMHIgv1c" heading="3"/>
    - The team uses the linked references of daily notes pages as a "table of contents" to monitor the team's work that week. Therefore, be judicious in how many times you reference a daily note with wikilinks. The top-level entry usually includes a reference to today's date, and any clear deadline can be referenced once per entry. Other dates should be labeled like `July 29` rather than with wikilinks. <roam uid="AJ-MJrH7M"/>
  - Reading nodes thoroughly <roam uid="UJfOc9mSn" heading="3"/>
    - When investigating a node, don't stop at the title. Read the template sections (Summary, Description, Rationale, etc.) for substance, and follow page references in the content for context. <roam uid="9mWl4_KbG"/>
    - All the firebase links are public links to images.  Usually, these images are very informative, so for relevant nodes and pages you should open the images and interpret them with your image recognition capabilities <roam uid="EIquKiNkw"/>
    - Check linked references to see where the node has been discussed in meetings, logs, and other nodes. <roam uid="rsCUVEZGn"/>
    - For Results and Evidence, pay attention to the Source in the title and the Grounding Context section for methodological detail. <roam uid="rxcu3DrEs"/>
  - Linking to this graph <roam uid="sTxa7aNev" heading="3"/>
    - If you create a URL in the agentic chat UI (outside of roam), remember that the URL starts with `https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/`. The graph url is discourse-graphs; the graph MCP nickname is dg-team. <roam uid="8VfrwIAkz"/>
  - Formatting <roam uid="DLi8zMdfk" heading="3"/>
    - When writing in Roam, you can make use of colors, color underlines, and comments: <roam uid="UPWoTfgXC"/>
      - [[>]] [[!NOTE]] This is a basic note callout\nNotes are great for highlighting general information you want to draw attention to. <roam uid="GRXCvlZXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!INFO]] Informational callout with an info icon\nUse these for additional context or background details. <roam uid="q9AGKeYbe"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUMMARY]] A summary or abstract callout\nPerfect for executive summaries, TLDRs, or condensed overviews. <roam uid="-e0ZjrNmx"/>
      - [[>]] [[!TIP]] Helpful tip — try using callouts for emphasis!\nCombine callouts with **bold**, *italic*, and `code` formatting in both the title and body. <roam uid="QZj72rl96"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUCCESS]] Operation completed successfully\nAll 47 tests passed. The deployment to staging is live. <roam uid="qnaPlXY2m"/>
      - [[>]] [[!QUESTION]] How do callouts work in Roam?\nThe first line after `[[!TYPE]]` is the title. Add body text on the next line with **Shift+Enter**. <roam uid="HQRN8neWv"/>
      - [[>]] [[!WARNING]] Be careful when editing shared pages\nOther users may be viewing or editing at the same time. <roam uid="tAydkxtXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!FAILURE]] Build failed due to missing dependencies\nRun `npm install` and check that all peer dependencies are satisfied. <roam uid="gzwZx-squ"/>
      - [[>]] [[!DANGER]] Do NOT delete this page — critical data\nThis page contains production configuration values referenced by multiple systems. <roam uid="22V2wAMnL"/>
      - [[>]] [[!BUG]] Found a rendering issue on mobile viewports\nThe sidebar overlaps the main content when screen width is below 768px. <roam uid="JmKFXi5jT"/>
      - [[>]] [[!EXAMPLE]] Here's how you format a callout\nUse `[[>]] [[!TYPE]] Title` on the first line. Add body text with Shift+Enter. <roam uid="cLHhp8Dwj"/>
      - [[>]] [[!QUOTE]] "The best way to predict the future is to invent it."\n— Alan Kay, 1971 <roam uid="ACj_6GA26"/>
      - **Foldable Callouts** <roam uid="aUAi8OGtt"/>
        - Add `+` or `-` after the type (e.g. `[[!TIP]]+`) to make it foldable. `+` starts expanded, `-` starts collapsed. Click the header to toggle. <roam uid="zle_pzhMf"/>
        - [[>]] [[!TIP]]+ Click to collapse this tip\nThis body is visible by default because of the `+` marker. It hides when you click the header. <roam uid="kSoteggqF"/>
        - [[>]] [[!WARNING]]- Hidden by default — click to expand\nThis body starts collapsed because of the `-` marker. Click the header to reveal it. <roam uid="ibBbriqTD"/>
      - **Headings + Callouts** <roam uid="PFTcFSNTv"/>
        - Callouts work inside heading blocks. The title scales with the heading size while the body stays regular size. <roam uid="iq3SyE9bG"/>
        - [[>]] [[!WARNING]] Heading callout\nBody text stays regular size. <roam uid="Y7N7Q52Dh" heading="2"/>

# Untitled - status - Copy of the OpenSpec change `headless-mcp-retrieval`, which supersedes ((LPDwCRT6_))[[OpenSpec]] output for Headless MCP retrieval. The files live in `openspec/changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/` in the repo and are not yet committed. `openspec validate --strict` passes. - {{[[TODO]]}} [[+Michael Gartner]] This spec has been reviewed and edited by me. Ready for your review. Feel free to put a time slot on my calendar from Thurs onward for detailed review. Alternatively, feel free to async review by tagging me in specfic parts - Proposal - Why - Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent without opening Roam or Obsidian, and without a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. The MCP uses a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin. - What Changes - **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service and the only backend of the MCP. - **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex. - **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M))), [options compared](((bTMUCrCnD)))): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])). - **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access, including shared nodes that were never imported into the client. - **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`. - **Search is semantic.** It reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC (database function), with type filtering and no relevance cutoff. - Capabilities - New Capabilities - `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context. - `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract. - `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution. - `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only. - Modified Capabilities - None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet. - Out of scope for v0 - A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API. - Option B, a separate agent account. - Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents. - Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering. - Keyword or hybrid search. It's proposed for after v0, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search) (design Decision 6). - One session that spans several spaces. - Impact - **`packages/database`:** - `mcp_reader` (read-only database role); - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in); - an `EXECUTE` allowlist (which database functions the role may call); - the space login lock (stops a session from replacing the space login); - retrieval functions built on the discovery converters; - one semantic search RPC (database function). - **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation. - **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm. - **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook and the space login lock (design Decision 4). - **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions) and sign-out. - **Builds on** [ENG-1985](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985) (database-to-node converter) and [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) (discovery returns shared nodes), both merged. They provide `dbNodeToCrossApp` (converts one node), `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) and `SharedNodeListing` (nodes plus their spaces). - Open decisions - Whether one agent should span several spaces. - Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` (the shared node format) and `rid` (global node ID) for the agent API ([Roam block](((SRa9xHk30)))). - No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet. - Design - Context - These facts from `origin/main` shape the design. - **Identity and data** - **Space accounts.** Each plugin signs in as its space's account using the **space login**, a random secret stored in the plugin (`signInWithPassword` in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`). There are no personal user accounts yet. - **Session handoff.** `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) lets the plugin use the space login to open one extra session, and hand that session's refresh token to the MCP. The MCP stores only that session, never the space login. Each handed-over session is recorded in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions). None of this is in the repo yet. - **Concepts and content.** - `Concept` (the node, type and relation table) holds node instances, schemas and relations, flagged by `is_schema` and `is_relation`. - `Content` (the text table) joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`. Its variants are `direct` (title), `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` (title plus description) and `full` (body). - **Readability.** The `my_*` views (views filtered to what the caller can read), and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express read access. - **Discovery and embeddings** - **Discovery.** [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) made discovery return shared nodes. - `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`: `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode` (shared node format). - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) reads one readable node by `rid` (global node ID). - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node types and relations into that format. - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full` (the body); import fetches it separately. - **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors, each with an `obsolete` flag. - `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter. - Sync embeds every node's title (`direct`), on both platforms. Roam embeds the title plus description instead (`direct_and_description`) when a node has a description. No platform embeds the body (`full`). - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`). - **Database access controls** - **Row-level security.** 58 of the 62 row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects` (file storage), which retrieval doesn't read. Table grants go to `authenticated` (the signed-in role) and `service_role`. `anon` holds `SELECT` on `Space`, the contributor tables and the `my_*` views, ahead of public access ([ENG-1837](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1837)). - **Function privileges.** Every function is granted explicitly. `authenticated` gets every new function by default, and `anon` gets only a listed set of read-only functions. `packages/database/doc/security_model.md` gives the rules and the heuristic for granting new functions. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` (they run as their owner, not as the caller), such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`. Each is granted to `authenticated` only. - **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` (a session token lasts one hour). The custom access token hook is commented out. - Goals / Non-Goals - **Goals:** - One retrieval service: every client, the MCP included, goes through the API. - Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules. - The database enforces the agent session's read-only access, not the MCP. - Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content. - **Non-Goals:** - A new identity system. - A hosted MCP. - A second embedding pipeline. - Attachment access. - Auditing. - Decisions - 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client - {{[[mermaid]]}} - flowchart LR - plugin["Roam / Obsidian plugin"] -- "connect command:
bundle with refresh token, shown once" --> connect["mcp connect
(one-time CLI step)"] - connect -- "saves the session" --> state[("Local state file")] - agent["Agent client
Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex"] -- "stdio" --> mcp["Local MCP"] - state --- mcp - mcp -- "HTTPS + session token" --> api["Retrieval API
apps/website /api/v1"] - api --> fns["Retrieval functions
packages/database"] - fns --> db[("Supabase Postgres
row-level security")] - api -- "search text only" --> emb["OpenAI embeddings API
turns query text into a vector"] - OpenAI here is only the embeddings service that turns a search query into a vector, the same one sync already uses. It isn't ChatGPT, which stays unsupported. - Each capability spec covers one layer: - {{[[mermaid]]}} - flowchart TB - agent["Agent client"] --> tools - subgraph mcpLayer["discourse-mcp: how agent clients reach the API"] - tools["Four MCP tools
pass API results through"] - end - subgraph apiLayer["headless-retrieval-api: how callers reach the operations"] - routes["API routes
HTTP, auth, envelope, versioning"] - end - subgraph coreLayer["discourse-retrieval: what the operations return"] - core["Retrieval functions
packages/database"] - end - tools --> routes --> core - session["agent-read-access:
the read-only session the MCP holds"] -.-> tools - **The API holds all retrieval logic.** It is four routes in `apps/website`. They call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies. - **The MCP** holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls the embeddings service. - **The contract is `/api/v1`** (the versioned route prefix). - Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`. - Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release. - **Alternatives:** - **The MCP reads the database directly.** - Installed copies would then depend on view shapes, and every fix would need an MCP release. - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth. - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity. - **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT but needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later. - 2. Reuse the discovery read path - The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database`. These build on Sid's discovery code from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091): - **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID), then fetches the `full` Content (the body) the way import does. - **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types). - **Discourse context** finds the readable relation instances that touch the node. - Candidates come from `refs`, the list of referenced IDs. - Direction comes from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content` (the relation's endpoint map). - Relations are converted with `dbRelationsToCrossApp` (converts relations). - Only search needs a new RPC (database function); see Decision 6. - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new RPCs, which would duplicate the converters. - 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access` - `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])) defines the handoff: - **Handoff.** - 1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes. - 2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`. - 3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy. - **Registry.** `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions) records the session ID (taken from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time. - **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope (only its own session). Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0. - **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login. - **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space. - **Tokens.** Two tokens are involved: - the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes; - the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use. - The bundle carries only the refresh token. So the holder's first session token comes from a refresh, and it already carries `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register. - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** Option B, a separate agent account for each grant, with a credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work. - 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2) - Under Option A2 ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M)))), the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API, so the database is what enforces read-only. - **The hook.** A custom access token hook (a database function Supabase calls on every token issue and refresh) checks the token's `session_id`. When the session is in `mcp_session` (list of handed-over sessions), it sets the token's `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (read-only database role; name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`. - **The role.** `mcp_reader`: - is granted to `authenticator` (the role Supabase's REST layer logs in as), so requests can switch to it; - has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`; - has `EXECUTE` only on an allowlist: the search RPC, plus the access helpers that the policies and views call. - **Granting functions.** The default privileges don't cover a new role, so `mcp_reader` starts with no `EXECUTE`. It gets an explicit allowlist: the search RPC, plus the existing helpers that the views and policies it reads call, such as `my_space_ids` and `my_accessible_resources`. The allowlist starts from `anon`'s read-only set, which public access already uses. Postgres checks a function called inside a view or policy against the querying role, so a missing grant fails the read with a permission error ([security model](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/main/packages/database/doc/security_model.md), rules 1-2). A new read function that retrieval reaches needs a grant to `mcp_reader` too. Plugin and sync grants don't change. - {{[[DONE]]}} [[+Marc-Antoine Parent]] Would you mind confirming this item? I checked whether revoking `EXECUTE` on `PUBLIC` role would affect current functionalities, but want to double check with you - **This doesn't change what plugins or sync can do.** `base.sql` runs first and sets default privileges that grant every later function to `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly. So the plugins' roles don't rely on `PUBLIC`, and they keep every function they can call today. Postgres has no deny grant, and every role inherits `PUBLIC`, so removing that default is the only way to keep a function from `mcp_reader`. Before the revoke, a check on the hosted database confirms that `anon` and `authenticated` hold `EXECUTE` on every function. Its migrations predate the schema files, so it could differ. - I just did a big cleanup of that. It includes a list of which functions needed to be revoked, or not, and why. I want anon to have access to some read-only functions, subject to RLS, so we can publish to everyone. - The list is in database/doc/security_model.md - It's not just a list, there's also heuristic to decide new functions. - Some of the discussion is in [ENG-2466: Set sensible default privileges and explicit grants in migrations​](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2466/set-sensible-default-privileges-and-explicit-grants-in-migrations) - It all is meant to accommodate the eventual [ENG-1837: Add a public status in the database​](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1837/add-a-public-status-in-the-database) - If you want to change some specific permissions, or question the heuristics, by all means to be discussed. But I want you to know what is there and why - A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so its reads follow the space account's current access. - **Supabase Auth requests aren't covered by the role.** A handed-over session could ask Auth to replace the space login, which would lock out the plugins and let it open sessions that can write. This change turns on the **space login lock** (`secure_password_change` and "require current password"), which refuses that without the current space login. A session could also sign out the plugins' sessions; the plugins just sign back in, and signing out the handed-over session ends it. - **A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. The MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`, which catches a misconfigured project at setup. - **Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (session token lifetime, 3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this. - **Alternative: plain Option A** (the agent signs in as the space account, with read-only enforced only in the MCP's tools). Any process holding the bundle could then write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP. - 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid` - **Identifiers** - **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid` (global node ID), built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`. - For an `http` space URI, it's `/`. - Otherwise, it's `orn:.note:…/`. - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone. - **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid`, from `getNodeTypeRid`, never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate. - **Payload** - **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s (shared node format) in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. - **Extra fields.** `DbCrossAppNode` carries IDs, not names, so each node also gets: - `type`: `{ rid, name }`, with the name from `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` (converts node types); - `author`: `{ name }`, from `PlatformAccount.name` through `my_accounts` (accounts the caller can see), because `authorId` is the platform's internal account ID; - `sourceUrl` for Roam nodes, built as `/page/`, or `sourcePath` for Obsidian nodes, from the `filePath` in the title row's metadata, since an Obsidian note has no stable web URL. - Search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type. - **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` (the body) as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML. - **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted. - **Provenance.** It's the author's name, the space's name, platform and URL (from the `spaces` entry), the created and modified times, and the source link or path. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault. - **Gaps are errors** - **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does. - **Get-node doesn't skip:** - `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`. - A conversion failure or a missing body maps to `content_unavailable`. - A stored empty body is not a missing row. - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id` (internal database row ID), which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity. - 6. Semantic search through one new RPC - **Embedding the query.** The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions. It uses the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. The MCP doesn't call the embedding route. - **The search RPC** (`SECURITY INVOKER`, so it runs as the caller) takes the query vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It: - joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` (title) and `direct_and_description` (title plus description) embeddings of readable node instances; - keeps each node's best similarity, once; - applies authorization, the type filter and deduplication before the limit; - sorts by similarity, then by `rid`; - has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible. - `score` is the cosine similarity. `match_content_embeddings` (the existing semantic search query) stays unchanged. - **Other behavior** - Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them. - Embedding failures are errors, not empty results. - **The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the body (`content.full`). When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct` (the title). The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched. - **Proposed for after v0: hybrid search.** Adapt [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). The recipe is a SQL function to copy, not a built-in. It: - ranks rows by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity; - merges the two rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. - Here it would need two schema additions on `Content` (the text table): a generated full-text column and a GIN index. The search RPC would gain a keyword list and a fusion step. The `/api/v1` search route keeps its inputs, so this is an additive change. Exact words such as names, acronyms and titles would then rank well even when the embedding misses them. - 7. One-hop discourse context - Return each readable relation instance that touches the node, with: - its `rid` (global node ID); - its type; - its direction; - a summary of the connected node. - Rules: - The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable. Relations are read through `my_concepts` (filtered to what the caller can read) with the caller's session, so an unreadable relation never comes back. Drop a relation whose type or endpoint the caller can't read before converting it, because `dbRelationsToCrossApp` throws on a missing endpoint instead of skipping it. - Keep relations distinct even when they share a label. - A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing. - Don't follow ordinary backlinks, and don't go past one hop. - 8. API contract - {{[[table]]}} - API route - MCP tool - Input - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` - `get_node` - node `rid` - `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` - `search_nodes` - query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit - `GET /api/v1/node-types` - `get_node_types` - none - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` - `get_discourse_context` - node `rid` - `rid`s (global node IDs) contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path. - **Each route does three things:** - 1. It validates the session token with Supabase Auth, then builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests. - 2. It validates the input with the shared Zod schemas (typed input and output definitions). - 3. It calls one `packages/database` function. - **Any session token is accepted.** The API accepts any valid space-account session token: a plugin's own session, or a handed-over one. The API exposes only reads, and the database keeps handed-over sessions read-only (Decision 4), so the API doesn't check the role. - **Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them: - the API validates requests with them; - the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them. - **Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. - **Internal reference.** A `README` next to the routes documents this contract for whoever maintains the MCP or the API. It isn't developer onboarding. - **Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`: - a blank query; - a malformed `rid`; - an explicitly empty type list; - a limit outside 1-30. - The default limit is 10. Unknown type `rid`s match nothing. - **Error codes:** - {{[[table]]}} - Code - HTTP status - When - `unauthenticated` - 401 - Token is missing, invalid or expired - `not_found` - 404 - Node is missing or unreadable - `content_unavailable` - 409 - Node lacks its body or can't be converted - `invalid_request` - 422 - Input fails validation - `result_too_large` - 422 - Response exceeds the budget - `dependency_error` - 503 - Database or embedding failure - The two 422 errors are told apart by the code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results. - **Response budget.** A response is either complete or fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to be validated in each client. - **Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header (which carries the session token), the query text or node bodies. - 9. The local MCP - **Tools.** - Each tool calls exactly one API operation. - It returns the API's result as structured content, plus a short text form. - It turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`. - Every tool is annotated read-only. - **Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the MCP protocol. - **Session** - **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name ` does the following: - reads the bundle from stdin; - refreshes once and checks that the role is `mcp_reader` (read-only database role); - writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/.json` with mode 0600. - The client config then holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token. - **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle. - **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process. Two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each one with its own bundle and `--name`. - **Distribution and setup** - **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`. - **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover: - the risk that the state file can read everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it; - one bundle per client; - search limits; - sync-gap errors; - that ChatGPT is unsupported. - Risks / Trade-offs - [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on. - [A switched-off hook fails open] → Handed-over sessions would get `authenticated`, which can write. The MCP's startup role check catches this. A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get a write-capable session. - [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. The API integration tests run every operation with a handed-over session, so as `mcp_reader`. - [A new read function isn't granted to `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails with a permission error once a policy or view starts calling it. The allowlist test and the API integration tests catch this. Add `mcp_reader` to the security model's checklist for new functions. - [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes. - [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`. - [Session tokens that can write pass through the website] → The API accepts plugin sessions too. Routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, up to one hour. - [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs. - [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space. - [Search covers titles, not bodies] → Every node's title is embedded, and Roam nodes with a description match on that too. A query that matches only a node's body won't find it, on either platform. Document this in the MCP setup docs. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist. Embedding more text needs a sync change and re-embedding, so it's out of v0. - [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports. - Migration Plan - 1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command). - 2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project. - 3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior. - 4. Deploy the API routes. - 5. Build and publish the MCP. - 6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort. - 7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay. - specs - `headless-retrieval-api` - Purpose - How callers reach the retrieval operations: HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract. The MCP calls the API on behalf of agent clients. What the operations return is specified in `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior). - ADDED Requirements - Requirement: Four retrieval operations - The system SHALL provide an HTTP API for four operations: get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` (retrieval behavior) contract. The API SHALL be the only retrieval backend for the MCP. - **Scenario: MCP calls each operation** - **WHEN** the MCP calls each of the four operations with a valid session token - **THEN** each operation applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules - **AND** no other retrieval path is required - Requirement: Response envelope - Every API response SHALL carry a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. An error SHALL NOT be returned as an empty `data` collection. - **Scenario: Failed request** - **WHEN** an operation fails - **THEN** the response has a request ID and an error object, with a stable code and a message that doesn't expose internals - **AND** the response has no `data` - Requirement: Authenticated sessions - The API SHALL accept a valid session token for a space account. It SHALL reject missing, invalid and expired tokens, and SHALL NOT store tokens between requests. The API SHALL expose only read operations. Read-only access for agent sessions is enforced by the database, as specified in `agent-read-access` (the agent's session). - **Scenario: Missing or expired token** - **WHEN** a request carries no token, or an expired one - **THEN** the API rejects it as unauthenticated, and returns no discourse data - Requirement: Versioned contract - The API SHALL serve its operations under a version prefix such as `/api/v1`. Changes within a version SHALL be additive. A breaking change SHALL ship under a new version, alongside the old one. - **Scenario: An installed MCP after a server change** - **GIVEN** an installed MCP built against `/api/v1` - **WHEN** the website deploys a change within `/api/v1` - **THEN** the installed MCP's requests keep working - Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup - After handoff and sync, the API SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian open. Responses SHALL come from the database's synced state. - **Scenario: Source application is closed** - **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a session token - **WHEN** Roam and Obsidian are closed, and a caller calls the API - **THEN** eligible synced data is returned - `discourse-retrieval` - Purpose - What the API's four retrieval operations return, whichever client calls them: which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery, and one-hop discourse context. All of it stays within the caller's current read access. The API exposes these operations over HTTP (`headless-retrieval-api`), and the MCP passes their results through (`discourse-mcp`). - ADDED Requirements - Requirement: Readable synced collection - All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the caller's space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application. - **Scenario: Readable but unimported node** - **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the caller, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client - **WHEN** the caller fetches it or searches for it - **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking - **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally - **Scenario: Unreadable node** - **WHEN** a caller requests a node it cannot read - **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata - Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid - Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` (global node ID), and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate. - **Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces** - **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim" - **WHEN** the caller discovers node types - **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s - Requirement: Full node text - Getting a readable node SHALL return its `rid` (global node ID), title, type and provenance (see "Readable type and provenance"), and its full synced text body. The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation. - **Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links** - **WHEN** a caller fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment - **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text - **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents - Requirement: Readable type and provenance - Every node an operation returns SHALL carry its type and its provenance in readable form: - its type, as the type's `rid` and name (for example "Claim"); - the author's name; - the space's name, platform and URL; - its created and modified times; - a link to open it at the source when the platform has one (a Roam page URL), or else its file path (an Obsidian vault path). - **Scenario: Readable type and author** - **GIVEN** a readable Claim node written by Trang in the "Lab" space - **WHEN** a caller fetches it - **THEN** the response names the type "Claim", the author "Trang" and the space "Lab", alongside the type's `rid` - Requirement: Semantic search over existing embeddings - Search SHALL rank nodes by semantic similarity using the stored embeddings, without re-embedding. Sync embeds every node's title, on both platforms. Roam also embeds the description with the title when a node has one. Bodies aren't embedded on either platform, so matching covers titles (and Roam descriptions), not full bodies. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking. - **Scenario: Matching by meaning** - **WHEN** a caller submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings - **THEN** a node can rank even when its title lacks the query's exact words - **Scenario: Titles on both platforms** - **GIVEN** a node whose titles both match the query's meaning - **WHEN** the caller searches - **THEN** both nodes can rank - **Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding** - **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description - **WHEN** the caller searches - **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking - **Scenario: Body-only changes** - **GIVEN** the title, description, permissions and filters are unchanged - **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes - **THEN** the node's search ranking doesn't change - Requirement: Search result fields - Each search result SHALL contain the node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type and provenance, plus a short excerpt and a relevance score, but not the full body. Results SHALL be ordered by relevance. - **Scenario: Result fields** - **WHEN** a search returns results - **THEN** each result has those fields, and the results are ordered by score - Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff - Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. Search SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints. - **Scenario: Default and explicit limits** - **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes - **WHEN** the caller searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20 - **THEN** the responses contain 10 results and 20 results - **AND** neither response offers a continuation page - **Scenario: Weak matches** - **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes that match the query weakly, and a limit of 10 - **WHEN** the caller searches - **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order - **Scenario: Limit above the maximum** - **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results - **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request - **Scenario: Empty eligible collection** - **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the caller's access and type constraints - **THEN** search returns an empty result - Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering - Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s (global type IDs) and names, only for types present on nodes the caller can currently read. That includes types on shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types. - **Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes** - **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes - **WHEN** the caller discovers node types - **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not - **Scenario: Multiple selected types** - **WHEN** the caller searches with types A and B selected - **THEN** every result has type A or B, and is readable by the caller - **Scenario: No type filter** - **WHEN** the caller searches without a type filter - **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type - Requirement: One-hop discourse context - Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give: - its type; - its direction relative to the requested node; - the connected node's `rid` (global node ID), title, type (`rid` and name), author name and space name. - Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately, through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT go past one hop. - **Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships** - **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B - **WHEN** the caller requests discourse context for A, and then for B - **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary - **Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink** - **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C - **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context - **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned - **Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls** - **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships from A to B and from B to C, and none from A to C - **WHEN** the caller requests A's discourse context - **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C - **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C - `agent-read-access` - Purpose - The session an agent holds. A plugin hands it over, it reads the space's synced discourse graph with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only. This follows Option A2 ([decision](((guIcK3Z9M)))): the agent signs in as the space account, but its session can't write. - ADDED Requirements - Requirement: Session handed over through `mcp-session-access` - The MCP SHALL use a session that a plugin handed over and registered through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec]([[Spec: MCP token handoff]])). No website session or agent-management page SHALL be required. The MCP SHALL NOT receive the space login, which is the credential plugins use to sign in. - **Scenario: Connect from either platform** - **WHEN** a user runs the connect command in a signed-in Roam or Obsidian client - **THEN** the plugin shows a bundle for a new, registered session of that client's space account - **AND** the plugin's own session is unchanged - Requirement: Per-space principal - The system SHALL treat the space account whose session was handed over as the principal, meaning the identity whose access is used. Retrieval SHALL use that account's readable collection. It SHALL NOT combine the access of other space accounts that the same person uses. Reading another space's synced but unpublished nodes SHALL require a bundle from that space. - **Scenario: Another space's private synced nodes** - **GIVEN** a person uses spaces A and B, and a node in B is not readable by A's space account - **WHEN** an agent uses a bundle from space A - **THEN** it cannot retrieve the node in B - **Scenario: Accessible shared node** - **GIVEN** a node from another space is readable by the space account through sharing - **WHEN** the agent retrieves that node - **THEN** the node is returned, even though the space account didn't import or author it - Requirement: Current permissions - The system SHALL evaluate retrieval against the space account's current read permissions. - Removing access SHALL stop later retrieval of the affected data. - Adding access SHALL make the affected synced data eligible. - Neither change SHALL require a new bundle. - **Scenario: Permissions change after handoff** - **WHEN** a space account gains access to node A and loses access to node B after a bundle is handed over - **THEN** later requests with that bundle can retrieve A and cannot retrieve B - Requirement: Session sign-out - The MCP SHALL be able to sign its own session out. A signed-out session SHALL NOT refresh. A session token the MCP already holds MAY stay valid until it expires, which is up to one hour. - **Scenario: Signed-out session** - **WHEN** a handed-over session is signed out - **THEN** the MCP cannot refresh it - **AND** requests fail once its current session token expires - Requirement: The database refuses writes from handed-over sessions - The database SHALL refuse every create, modify or delete made with a handed-over session, whichever client makes it. That includes calls to write functions. The session SHALL keep the space account's read access, and plugin sessions SHALL keep their permissions. Missing or expired sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval. - **Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools** - **GIVEN** a process holds a handed-over session, and the space account can edit a node - **WHEN** the process modifies the node, or calls a write function, directly with that session - **THEN** the database refuses it - **AND** the node remains unchanged - **Scenario: Plugin session keeps write access** - **GIVEN** a plugin has handed over a session - **WHEN** the plugin writes with its own session - **THEN** the write succeeds - **Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval** - **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing or expired session - **THEN** no discourse data is returned - Requirement: Handed-over sessions cannot replace the space login - A handed-over session SHALL NOT be able to replace the space login, which is the credential plugins use to sign in, using only its session token. - **Scenario: Agent tries to replace the space login** - **WHEN** a process asks Supabase Auth to set a new space login, using a handed-over session token - **THEN** Supabase Auth refuses the request - **AND** the space's plugins still sign in with the existing space login - `discourse-mcp` - Purpose - This spec covers how agent clients reach the retrieval API: through one local MCP that works with both Roam and Obsidian. The MCP runs on the user's machine, using a session the plugin hands over. If the operation fails, the tool SHALL return a tool error with the same code. - The MCP SHALL NOT read the database or call an embedding service itself. - **Scenario: Tool discovery** - **WHEN** an agent client lists the MCP's tools - **THEN** it sees exactly the four retrieval tools, each with its input definition and a read-only annotation - **Scenario: API error** - **WHEN** the API returns an error for a tool call - **THEN** the tool returns an error with the same code, not an empty result - **Scenario: API unreachable** - **WHEN** the API can't be reached - **THEN** the tool returns a dependency error - **Scenario: Agent asks the MCP to modify a node** - **WHEN** an agent asks the MCP to modify a node - **THEN** no MCP tool can perform the modification - Requirement: Distribution and setup - The MCP SHALL install from npm.
