They shouldn't need a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API, and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. Both use a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin. - What Changes - **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. - It is the one retrieval service: documented for developers, and the only backend of the MCP. - It accepts only handed-over sessions. - **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex. - **Identity follows Option A2**, decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The caller holds its own session of the space account, handed over through `mcp-session-access`, and the database makes that session read-only. - **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access. That includes shared nodes that were never imported into the client. - **Node shape.** Nodes are `DbCrossAppNode`s identified by `rid`. They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`. - **Search** reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC, with type filtering and no relevance cutoff. The API embeds queries on the server. - Capabilities - New Capabilities - `headless-retrieval-api`: the retrieval service. It provides the four operations over HTTP, accepts only handed-over sessions, and keeps a versioned contract. - `discourse-retrieval`: the behavior of those operations: node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context. - `agent-read-access`: the handed-over session as principal, its current read access, and database-enforced read-only. - `discourse-mcp`: the local MCP as a client of the API. Covers tool mapping, session handling, distribution and setup, and the supported clients. - Modified Capabilities - None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet. - Out of scope for v0 - A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API. - A separate agent principal (Option B). - Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents. - Multi-hop traversal, keyword or hybrid search, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering. - One session that spans several spaces. - Impact - **`packages/database`:** - the `mcp_reader` role; - a custom access token hook; - an `EXECUTE` allowlist for functions; - the space login lock; - retrieval functions built on the CrossApp converters; - one search RPC. - **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation. - **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm. - **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook, and the space login lock (design Decision 4). - **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** ([[Spec: MCP token handoff]]) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry and sign-out. - **Builds on ENG-1985 and ENG-2091** (merged): `dbNodeToCrossApp`, `getSharedNodeByRid` and `SharedNodeListing`. - Open decisions - Whether one agent should span several spaces. - Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` and `rid` for the agent API (((SRa9xHk30))). - No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet. - Design - Context - These facts from `origin/main` shape the design. - **Identity and data** - **Space accounts.** Plugins sign in as a per-space account with `signInWithPassword` (`packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`). This spec calls that credential the **space login**. It's a random secret stored in the plugin; there are no personal user accounts yet. `mcp-session-access` adds the handoff and the `mcp_session` registry; none of it is in the repo yet. - **Concepts and content.** `Concept` holds node instances, schemas and relations (`is_schema`, `is_relation`). `Content` joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`, with variants `direct`, `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` and `full`. - **Readability.** The `my_*` views, and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express what a caller can read. - **Discovery and embeddings** - **Discovery (ENG-2091).** `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`, which is `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode`. - `getSharedNodeByRid` reads one readable node by `rid`. - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node schemas and relations. - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full`; import fetches it separately. - **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors with an `obsolete` flag. - `match_content_embeddings` applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter. - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`). - Roam embeds `direct_and_description` when a node has a description, and `direct` otherwise. - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`). - **Database access controls** - **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 policies have no `TO` clause. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects`, which retrieval does not read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` and `service_role`. - **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` can execute every function in `public`, because no schema file revokes the default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`, such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`, so table grants alone don't stop them. - **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` and leaves the custom access token hook commented out. - Goals / Non-Goals - **Goals:** - One retrieval service. Every client, the MCP included, goes through the API. - Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules. - The database, not the API or the MCP, enforces read-only. - Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content. - **Non-Goals:** - A new identity system. - A hosted MCP. - A second embedding pipeline. - Attachment access. - Auditing. - Decisions - 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client - ```plain text\nRoam / Obsidian --connect command--> bundle (shown once)\n |\n npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --> local state file\n |\nagent client --stdio--> local MCP (thin client)\n |\n | HTTPS + session token\n v\ndeveloper ----------> apps/website /api/v1 --+--> packages/database functions --> Supabase as mcp_reader\n +--> OpenAI (search queries only)\n``` - The API holds all retrieval logic. - **Routes.** It's four routes in `apps/website` that call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies. - **MCP.** The MCP holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls OpenAI. - **Developers** call the same routes directly. - **The contract is `/api/v1`.** Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`. Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release. - **Alternatives:** - **The MCP reads the database directly.** - Installed copies would then depend on the view shapes, and fixes would need an MCP release. - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth. - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity. - **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT, but it needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later. - 2. Reuse the discovery read path - The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database` that build on Sid's discovery code: - **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid`, then fetches the `full` Content the way import does. - **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`. - **Discourse context** reads the readable relation instances whose `refs` contain the node. It takes direction from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content`, and converts the relations with `dbRelationsToCrossApp`. - Only search needs a new RPC (Decision 6). - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new `SECURITY INVOKER` RPCs. They duplicate the converters. - 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access` - `mcp-session-access` defines the handoff. - **Handoff.** - 1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes. - 2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`. - 3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy. - **Registry.** `mcp_session` records the session ID (from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time. - **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope. Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0. - **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login. - **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space. - **Tokens.** Two tokens are involved: - the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes; - the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use. - The bundle carries only the refresh token, so the holder's first session token comes from a refresh and already carries `mcp_reader` (Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register. - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** a separate Supabase auth user for each agent grant (Option B), with an opaque credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work. - 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2) - The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API. So the database, not the API, enforces read-only. - **The hook.** A custom access token hook runs on every token issue and refresh. When the token's `session_id` is in `mcp_session`, it sets the `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`. - **The role.** `mcp_reader`: - is granted to `authenticator`, so PostgREST can switch to it; - has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`; - has `EXECUTE` on an allowlist: the search RPC, and the access helpers that the policies and views call. - **Locking down functions.** Because `PUBLIC` holds `EXECUTE` on every function, the allowlist needs two changes: - `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`; - the matching default-privilege change. - `anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so reads follow the space account's current access. - **Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow: - **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has. - **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in. - **A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. Two checks catch a misconfigured project: - the API rejects any token whose `role` isn't `mcp_reader`; - the MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`. - **Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this. - **Alternative: plain A**, where only the tools are read-only. Any process holding the bundle could write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP. - 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid` - **Identifiers** - **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid`, built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`. - For an `http` space URI it's `/`. Otherwise it's `orn:.note:…/`. - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone. - **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid` (`getNodeTypeRid`), never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate. - **Payload** - **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. - **Added fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`; search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type. - **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML. - **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted. - **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault. - **Gaps are errors** - **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does. - **Get-node doesn't skip:** - `getSharedNodeByRid` returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`; - a conversion failure or a missing `full` Content maps to `content_unavailable`. - A stored empty body is not a missing row. - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id`, which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity. - 6. Search reuses stored vectors through one new RPC - The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions, using the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route. - The new `SECURITY INVOKER` RPC takes a vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It: - joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` and `direct_and_description` embeddings of readable node instances; - keeps each node's best similarity, once; - applies authorization, type filter and deduplication before the limit; - sorts by similarity, then `rid`; - has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible. - **Other behavior** - `match_content_embeddings` stays unchanged. - Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them. - Embedding failures are errors, not empty results. - **The excerpt** is the first 300 Unicode code points of the full body. When the body is missing, it falls back to `content.direct`. The excerpt isn't evidence that the body matched. - 7. One-hop discourse context - Return each readable relation instance that touches the node. Give its `rid`, type and direction, and a summary of the connected node. - The relation, its type and both endpoints must be readable. - Keep separate relations distinct, even when they share a label. - A self-link appears as both incoming and outgoing. - Don't follow ordinary backlinks or go past one hop. - 8. API contract - {{[[table]]}} - API route - MCP tool - Input - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` - `get_node` - node `rid` - `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` - `search_nodes` - query, optional type `rid`s, optional limit - `GET /api/v1/node-types` - `get_node_types` - none - `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` - `get_discourse_context` - node `rid` - `rid`s contain `/` and `:`, so they go URL-encoded in the path. - **Each route:** - 1. Validates the session token with Supabase Auth, and builds a request-scoped client that acts as the caller. Nothing is held between requests. - 2. Rejects the request with `unauthenticated` unless the token's `role` claim is `mcp_reader`. The website never carries a token that can write. - 3. Validates the input with the shared Zod schemas, then calls one `packages/database` function. - **Zod schemas.** The input and output schemas live in `packages/database`, so the API and the MCP share them: - the API validates requests with them; - the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them; - the API docs are checked against them. - **Response envelope.** Every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. - **Validation.** Reject the following with `invalid_request`: - a blank query; - a malformed `rid`; - an explicitly empty type list; - a limit outside 1-30. - The default limit is 10, and unknown type `rid`s match nothing. - **Error codes:** - {{[[table]]}} - Code - HTTP status - When - `unauthenticated` - 401 - Token is missing, invalid or expired, or isn't from a handed-over session - `not_found` - 404 - Node is missing or unreadable - `content_unavailable` - 409 - Node lacks its full Content or can't be converted - `invalid_request` - 422 - Input fails validation - `result_too_large` - 422 - Response exceeds the budget - `dependency_error` - 503 - Database or embedding failure - The two 422 errors are told apart by the error code in the envelope. Errors are never returned as empty results. - **Response budget.** A response is complete, or it fails with `result_too_large`. The proposed budget is 1 MiB serialized, to validate in each client. - **Logs** hold only the request ID, operation, duration, result count and error category. They never include the `Authorization` header, query text or node bodies. - 9. The local MCP - **Tools.** Each tool calls exactly one API operation. It returns the API's result as structured content plus a short text form, and it turns API errors into tool errors with the same code. An unreachable API is a `dependency_error`. Every tool is annotated read-only. - **Runtime.** Logs go to stderr, because stdout carries the protocol. - **Session** - **Connect.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp connect --name ` reads the bundle from stdin. It refreshes once, checks that the role is `mcp_reader`, and writes the session to `~/.discourse-graphs/mcp/.json` with mode 0600. Client config holds only the launch command and `--name`, never a token. - **Refresh.** The MCP refreshes against Supabase Auth. It writes each rotated refresh token to the state file atomically, before using the new session token. If the state file is lost, the user connects again with a new bundle. - **One process per connection.** A lock file next to the state file stops a second process, because two processes refreshing the same token can make Supabase revoke the session. A user with two clients connects each with its own bundle and `--name`. - **Token for developers.** `npx @discourse-graphs/mcp token --name ` prints a current session token for that connection, refreshing it under the lock. A developer connects with their own bundle and never handles refresh-token rotation. - **Distribution and setup** - **Package.** `@discourse-graphs/mcp` (name proposed), published to npm from `apps/mcp` with semver releases. Setup docs launch it with `npx -y @discourse-graphs/mcp@latest`. - **Per-client setup** is documented for Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The docs also cover: - the risk that the state file reads everything the space can read, and that any process running as the user can read it; - one bundle per client; - search limits; - sync-gap errors; - that ChatGPT is unsupported. - Risks / Trade-offs - [The hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup on `mcp_session`, return other claims unchanged, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook on. - [A switched-off hook fails open] → The API and the MCP both check the `role` claim (Decision 4). A harness that calls Supabase directly would still get `authenticated`. - [A grant is missing from `mcp_reader`] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`. - [Revoking from `PUBLIC` breaks a function that relied on it] → Run the full cucumber suite as `anon` and `authenticated` after the revoke. - [The MCP depends on the website] → If the website is down, MCP retrieval fails with `dependency_error`, and every call takes one extra network hop. Accepted, in exchange for one contract and server-side fixes. - [`/api/v1` is pinned by installed copies] → Change it only additively. A breaking change ships as `/api/v2` alongside `v1`. - [Session tokens pass through the website] → Only read-only session tokens are accepted, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs. A leaked session token stays valid until it expires, up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s). - [The state file is readable by any process running as the user] → Accepted for v0, and stated in the setup docs. - [One session reads one space] → A user with several spaces adds one MCP entry per space. - [Embedding inputs differ by platform] → Document the difference. Test correctness with deterministic vector fixtures, and tune relevance once real queries exist. - [Shared nodes look unfamiliar] → Label provenance as origin, and say that results reflect readable synced data, not local imports. - Migration Plan - 1. Land `mcp-session-access` (registry, handoff helper and connect command). - 2. Add `mcp_reader`, the function allowlist and the access token hook, and turn on the space login lock. Enable the hook and the lock on the hosted project. - 3. Add the retrieval functions and the search RPC through the declarative schema workflow. Existing RPCs and clients keep their behavior. - 4. Deploy the API routes. - 5. Build and publish the MCP. - 6. Validate in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with Roam and Obsidian closed, then release to a limited cohort. - 7. To roll back, deprecate the npm package, disable the routes, and sign out the registered sessions. The additive role, functions and RPC can stay. - Open Questions - Whether one agent should span several spaces. - Example queries for docs, and a relevance evaluation set. Neither changes the architecture. - specs - `headless-retrieval-api` - Purpose - Provide the retrieval service: four read-only operations over HTTP, which developers call directly and the MCP calls on behalf of agent clients. - ADDED Requirements - Requirement: Four retrieval operations - The system SHALL provide an HTTP API for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` and `agent-read-access` contracts. The API SHALL be the only retrieval backend for the MCP. - **Scenario: Developer calls each operation directly** - **WHEN** a developer calls each of the four operations with a valid handed-over session - **THEN** each operation applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules - **AND** no MCP is required - Requirement: Response envelope - Every API response SHALL carry a request ID. It SHALL also carry either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. An error SHALL NOT be returned as an empty `data` collection. - **Scenario: Failed request** - **WHEN** an operation fails - **THEN** the response has a request ID and an error object with a stable code and a message that doesn't expose internals - **AND** the response has no `data` - Requirement: Handed-over sessions only - The API SHALL accept only a session token from a handed-over session, which carries the read-only database role. It SHALL reject missing, invalid and expired tokens, and tokens from any other session, including plugin sessions. It SHALL NOT store tokens between requests. - **Scenario: Plugin session token** - **WHEN** a request carries a valid session token from a plugin's own session - **THEN** the API rejects it, and returns no discourse data - **Scenario: Missing or expired token** - **WHEN** a request carries no token, or an expired one - **THEN** the API rejects it as unauthenticated - Requirement: Versioned contract - The API SHALL serve its operations under a version prefix. Changes within a version SHALL be additive. A breaking change SHALL ship under a new version, alongside the old one. - **Scenario: An installed MCP after a server change** - **GIVEN** an installed MCP built against `/api/v1` - **WHEN** the website deploys a change within `/api/v1` - **THEN** the installed MCP's requests keep working - Requirement: Documented developer contract - The API documentation SHALL cover: - authentication, including how to get a token; - inputs and outputs; - errors; - search limits; - type-filter semantics; - the per-space access model. - It SHALL also explain that: - readable unimported nodes can appear; - the existing embeddings determine semantic coverage; - search can return weak matches; - v0 search has no pagination. - **Scenario: Set up a direct integration** - **WHEN** a developer follows the API documentation with a handed-over session - **THEN** the documentation gives a working example for each of the four operations, and explains their results and errors - Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup - After handoff and sync, the API SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian open. Responses SHALL come from the database's synced state. - **Scenario: Source application is closed** - **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a handed-over session - **WHEN** Roam and Obsidian are closed, and a caller calls the API - **THEN** eligible synced data is returned - `discourse-retrieval` - Purpose - Let agents retrieve synced discourse node text, search by meaning with the existing embeddings, discover node types, and follow explicit one-hop discourse context, all within current read access. - ADDED Requirements - Requirement: Readable synced collection - All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the handed-over space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application. - **Scenario: Readable but unimported node** - **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the principal, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client - **WHEN** the agent fetches it or searches for it - **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking - **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally - **Scenario: Unreadable node** - **WHEN** an agent requests a node that its principal cannot read - **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata - Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid - Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate. - **Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces** - **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim" - **WHEN** the agent discovers node types - **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s - Requirement: Full node text - Getting a readable node SHALL return its `rid`, title, type `rid`, full synced text body, and provenance. The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation. - **Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links** - **WHEN** an agent fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment - **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text - **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents - Requirement: Existing semantic search - Search SHALL reuse the stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings, and SHALL NOT require re-embedding. Matching SHALL reflect the existing embedding inputs; it doesn't promise full-body coverage. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking. Each result SHALL contain the node's `rid`, title, type `rid`, a short excerpt and provenance, ordered by relevance. - **Scenario: Semantic search results** - **WHEN** an agent submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings - **THEN** results are ranked by semantic similarity and include the required fields - **AND** no node is excluded only because its title lacks the query's exact words - **Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding** - **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description - **WHEN** the agent searches - **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking - **Scenario: Unembedded body changes** - **GIVEN** embeddings, permissions and filters are unchanged - **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes - **THEN** its semantic matching score doesn't change - Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff - Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. It SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints. - **Scenario: Default and explicit limits** - **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes - **WHEN** the agent searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20 - **THEN** the responses contain 10 and 20 results - **AND** neither response offers a continuation page - **Scenario: Weak matches** - **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes with weak similarity, and a limit of 10 - **WHEN** the agent searches - **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order - **Scenario: Limit above the maximum** - **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results - **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request - **Scenario: Empty eligible collection** - **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the principal's access and type constraints - **THEN** search returns an empty result - Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering - Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s and names only for types present on nodes the principal can currently read, including shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types. - **Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes** - **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes - **WHEN** the agent discovers node types - **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not - **Scenario: Multiple selected types** - **WHEN** the agent searches with types A and B selected - **THEN** every result has type A or B and is readable by the principal - **Scenario: No type filter** - **WHEN** the agent searches without a type filter - **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type - Requirement: One-hop discourse context - Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give its type, its direction relative to the requested node, and the connected node's `rid`, title and type `rid`. Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT traverse past one hop. - **Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships** - **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B - **WHEN** the agent requests discourse context for A, and then for B - **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary - **Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink** - **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C - **WHEN** the agent requests A's discourse context - **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned - **Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls** - **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships A to B and B to C, and none from A to C - **WHEN** the agent requests A's discourse context - **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C - **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C - `agent-read-access` - Purpose - Let an agent read a space's synced discourse graph through its own read-only session of the space account. - ADDED Requirements - Requirement: Session handed over through `mcp-session-access` - The MCP SHALL use a session that a plugin handed over and registered through `mcp-session-access`. No website session or agent-management page SHALL be required. The MCP SHALL NOT receive the space login. - **Scenario: Connect from either platform** - **WHEN** a user runs the connect command in a signed-in Roam or Obsidian client - **THEN** the plugin shows a bundle for a new, registered session of that client's space account - **AND** the plugin's own session is unchanged - Requirement: Per-space principal - The system SHALL treat the space account whose session was handed over as the principal. Retrieval SHALL use that account's readable collection. It SHALL NOT combine the access of other space accounts that the same person uses. Reading another space's synced but unpublished nodes SHALL require a bundle from that space. - **Scenario: Another space's private synced nodes** - **GIVEN** a person uses spaces A and B, and a node in B is not readable by A's space account - **WHEN** an agent uses a bundle from space A - **THEN** it cannot retrieve the node in B - **Scenario: Accessible shared node** - **GIVEN** a node from another space is readable by the space account through sharing - **WHEN** the agent retrieves that node - **THEN** the node is returned, even though the space account didn't import or author it - Requirement: Current permissions - The system SHALL evaluate retrieval against the space account's current read permissions. Removing access SHALL stop later retrieval of the affected data. Adding access SHALL make the affected synced data eligible. Neither SHALL require a new bundle. - **Scenario: Permissions change after handoff** - **WHEN** a space account gains access to node A and loses access to node B after a bundle is handed over - **THEN** later requests with that bundle can retrieve A and cannot retrieve B - Requirement: Session sign-out - The MCP SHALL be able to sign its own session out. A signed-out session SHALL NOT refresh. A session token it already holds MAY stay valid until it expires. - **Scenario: Signed-out session** - **WHEN** a handed-over session is signed out - **THEN** the MCP cannot refresh it - **AND** requests fail once its current session token expires - Requirement: The database refuses writes from handed-over sessions - The database SHALL refuse every create, modify or delete made with a handed-over session, whichever client makes it. That includes calls to write functions. The session SHALL keep the space account's read access. Plugin sessions SHALL keep their permissions. Missing or expired sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval. - **Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools** - **GIVEN** a process holds a handed-over session, and the space account can edit a node - **WHEN** the process modifies the node or calls a write function directly with that session - **THEN** the database refuses it - **AND** the node remains unchanged - **Scenario: Plugin session keeps write access** - **GIVEN** a plugin has handed over a session - **WHEN** the plugin writes with its own session - **THEN** the write succeeds - **Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval** - **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing or expired session - **THEN** no discourse data is returned - Requirement: Handed-over sessions cannot replace the space login - A handed-over session SHALL NOT be able to replace the space login with only its session token. - **Scenario: Agent tries to replace the space login** - **WHEN** a process asks Supabase Auth to set a new space login, using a handed-over session token - **THEN** Supabase Auth refuses the request - **AND** the space's plugins still sign in with the existing space login - `discourse-mcp` - Purpose - Expose the retrieval API to agent clients through one local MCP, for both Roam and Obsidian. The MCP runs on the user's machine with a session the plugin hands over. - ADDED Requirements - Requirement: Tools are thin clients of the API - The MCP SHALL expose tools for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context, and no other tools. Each tool SHALL call exactly one operation of the retrieval API. It SHALL return that operation's result, and SHALL turn the operation's error into a tool error with the same code. The MCP SHALL NOT read the database or call an embedding service itself. - **Scenario: Tool discovery** - **WHEN** an agent client lists the MCP's tools - **THEN** it sees exactly the four retrieval tools, each with its input definition and a read-only annotation - **Scenario: API error** - **WHEN** the API returns an error for a tool call - **THEN** the tool returns an error with the same code, not an empty result - **Scenario: API unreachable** - **WHEN** the API can't be reached - **THEN** the tool returns a dependency error - **Scenario: Agent asks the MCP to modify a node** - **WHEN** an agent asks the MCP to modify a node - **THEN** no MCP tool can perform the modification - Requirement: Distribution and setup - The MCP SHALL install from npm. It SHALL take the bundle through a connect step that stores the session outside the agent client's configuration. It SHALL persist every rotated refresh token. It SHALL refuse to run a second process for the same connection. It SHALL refuse to start when its session lacks the read-only database role. - **Scenario: Connect stores the session locally** - **WHEN** a user runs the connect step with a bundle - **THEN** the session is stored in a local state file that only the user can read - **AND** the agent client's configuration holds no token - **Scenario: Restart after a refresh** - **GIVEN** the MCP has refreshed its session at least once - **WHEN** the agent client restarts the MCP - **THEN** the MCP resumes with the latest refresh token - **Scenario: Second process for one connection** - **WHEN** a second MCP process starts for a connection that is already running - **THEN** it exits with a clear error, and does not refresh the session - **Scenario: Read-only role missing** - **WHEN** the MCP's session token doesn't carry the read-only role - **THEN** the MCP refuses to start, and reports a project configuration error - Requirement: Supported agent clients - V0 SHALL document setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex. All four operations SHALL work in each of them, with Roam and Obsidian closed. Verify: cohort members complete setup and run all four operations before a wider release. - Follow-ups outside this change - Archive with `/opsx:archive` once every group has landed. - Decide whether one agent should span several spaces. - Proposal - Why - Users need to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent interface without opening Roam or Obsidian during retrieval or installing a platform-specific MCP for each. This v0 makes that collection available through a local MCP and a documented direct API, using a space account session handed over by the plugin. - What Changes - Provide four read-only operations through both interfaces: get a node, search nodes, discover node types, and get discourse context. The MCP is local: users install it, and the agent client launches it on their machine. Validate setup and these operations in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. ChatGPT cannot launch a local MCP and is not supported in v0. - The plugin hands the agent its own session for the space account, as specified in `mcp-session-access`. The agent acts as the space (Option A2): the session keeps the space account's read access, and the database refuses writes made with it. The MCP's tools and the API's operations also expose only retrieval. - Retrieve every synced discourse node readable by the space account, including accessible shared nodes that have never been imported into the client. Permissions follow current access: new access becomes available and removed access stops working. Signing out a handed-over session stops it from refreshing; access tokens it already holds stay valid until they expire. - Use per-space sessions as the v0 identity model. Access to another space's synced but unpublished nodes requires a bundle from that space. This does not promise one credential representing a person's combined access across spaces. - Return node ID, title, type, full synced text body, and source/provenance link when fetching a node. Attachment downloads and image/file contents are excluded. - Reuse the existing semantic search functionality and stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings. V0 does not require title-only re-embedding. Hybrid search, including keyword indexing and reciprocal rank fusion, is deferred to a later release. Return node ID, title, type, short excerpt, and source/provenance link, ordered by relevance. - Default search to 10 results, allow at most 30, and omit pagination. Apply no relevance cutoff in v0: weak matches may be returned. Empty results mean no eligible searchable nodes under the access and filter constraints, not a judgment that nothing is relevant. - Discover types present on currently readable nodes. Accept an optional filter of one or more type IDs, matching any selected type; omission searches all types. Further search-scope toggles and filters are deferred. - Return discourse context as incoming and outgoing one-hop explicit discourse relationships, including relationship type/direction and connected-node ID, title, and type. Return only relationships with two readable endpoints; retrieve connected bodies separately. Ordinary backlinks are excluded. - Boundaries and known limitations - Retrieval reads already-synced data. Candidate-node ingestion/retrieval, general non-discourse content, canvas functions, write-back, relation creation, candidate elevation, feedback capture, arbitrary-depth server traversal, and imported-only filtering are outside v0. Agents may repeat one-hop calls. - Accessible but unimported results may feel unfamiliar or outside the user's working collection. Results must not imply local import membership. Tracking that membership is not a v0 dependency. Semantic coverage follows the existing embedding inputs, which differ by platform and node representation; information absent from those inputs does not directly contribute to matching. Real-query evaluation examples and relevance thresholds are deferred. - A separate agent principal (Option B), a hosted MCP, and ChatGPT support are outside v0. Signing out a session takes effect when its current access token expires, not immediately. - Capabilities - New Capabilities - `agent-read-access`: Plugin-initiated session handoff, the space account as principal and its current read access, and database-enforced read-only access for handed-over sessions. - `discourse-retrieval`: Node payloads, semantic search using existing embeddings, readable-type discovery/filtering, and authorized one-hop discourse context. - `headless-retrieval-api`: Documented direct access to the four operations using the space account session and shared retrieval/access rules. - `discourse-mcp`: Local MCP delivery of the same operations, validated in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. - Modified Capabilities - None; the repository currently has no existing OpenSpec capability specs. - Impact - Expected affected areas are the narrow retrieval RPCs and integration with existing semantic search in `packages/database`, a new local MCP package, the connect command in `apps/roam` and `apps/obsidian` (through `mcp-session-access`), and `apps/website` as the host of the direct API routes and the query embedding route. This change depends on `mcp-session-access`, specified in the Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff` and not yet in this repository. It also depends on the shared CrossApp contracts in `packages/database`: `DbCrossAppNode`, the `dbNodeToCrossApp` converter (ENG-1985) and the `{ nodes, spaces }` listing envelope (ENG-2091). Node payloads use these contracts, and the `rid` is the node ID (design.md, Decision 5). Read-only is enforced by a read-only database role that a Supabase access token hook assigns to handed-over sessions, so `packages/database` also gains that role and hook. ENG-2057's feasibility evaluation of read-only delegation is input to it. The separate agent-access experiment is a design input, not evidence of deployed behavior or approval of its broader storage-read scope. - Open decisions and dependencies - **All hands (resolved 2026-11-10):** a local MCP, and Option A2 for agent identity. The per-space baseline stands; whether one agent should span several spaces is open. - **Decision record:** the 2026-11-10 notes record option A2. The spec owner chose A on 2026-11-12, then adopted A2 on 2026-11-13 after checking the meeting recording. See design.md, Decision 4. - **Node representation:** reusing `CrossAppNode` and `rid` for the agent API is pending Michael's confirmation. - **Design:** Credential-bearing MCP URLs are removed.
